WHY: backend/src/middlewares/auth.ts line 14 contains `console.log(token)` which prints raw Bearer tokens to stdout. In production this leaks JWT secrets into log aggregation systems (CloudWatch, Datadog, etc.), violating least-privilege and potentially exposing user sessions.

title: Add request rate limiting on /api/auth routes

WHY: The /api/auth routes (signup, login, reset-password, verify-email) have no rate limiting. An attacker can brute-force passwords or spam account creation. express-rate-limit is the standard lightweight solution for Express.

WHAT: Install express-rate-limit. Create a dedicated authRateLimiter instance (windowMs: 15 minutes, max: 20 requests per IP, standardHeaders: true, legacyHeaders: false, message: { message: 'Too many requests, please try again later.' }). Apply it in backend/src/routes/auth.ts before all route handlers using `router.use(authRateLimiter)`.

Acceptance criteria:

- After 20 requests from the same IP within 15 minutes to any /api/auth route, subsequent requests receive HTTP 429 with the configured message.
- RateLimit-* response headers are present on auth responses.
- Non-auth routes are unaffected.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

title: Harden CORS configuration in app.ts
description:
WHY: The current CORS config in backend/src/app.ts uses `callback(null, true)` for all origins, meaning any website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to the API. This enables CSRF-style attacks from arbitrary origins.

WHAT: Replace the open-origin callback with an explicit allowlist. Read allowed origins from a CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS environment variable (comma-separated). Fall back to ['http://localhost:3000'] in development. If an incoming origin is not in the allowlist, call `callback(new Error('CORS: origin not allowed'))`. Keep credentials: true and existing methods/allowedHeaders.

Acceptance criteria:
- A request from an origin not in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS receives a CORS error (no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header).
- A request from an allowed origin receives Access-Control-Allow-Origin matching that origin.
- Requests with no origin header (mobile/curl) are still allowed (pass null origin through).
- CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS env var is documented in backend/.env.example or README.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

Files to touch:
- backend/src/app.ts
- backend/.env.example (or root .env.example)

Acceptance criteria:
- A JSON POST body larger than 256 KB returns HTTP 413 Entity Too Large.
- Normal API requests under 256 KB are unaffected.

title: Add helmet security headers middleware
description:
WHY: The backend sends no security-related HTTP response headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.), making it vulnerable to clickjacking and MIME-sniffing attacks.

WHAT: Install the helmet package. Add `app.use(helmet())` near the top of backend/src/app.ts, before the CORS and route middleware. Configure helmet to not set HSTS in development (check NODE_ENV). The /docs route serving Swagger UI needs `contentSecurityPolicy: false` because Swagger UI loads inline scripts; use `app.use('/docs', helmet({ contentSecurityPolicy: false }))` before the general helmet call, or configure a specific CSP that allows swagger-ui-bundle.js from the CDN.

Acceptance criteria:
- Response headers include X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, and Referrer-Policy.
- GET /docs still renders Swagger UI correctly (not broken by CSP).
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

title: Improve error handler to suppress stack traces in production
description:
WHY: backend/src/middlewares/errorHandler.ts currently calls `console.error(err)` which prints the full error including stack trace to stdout, and returns err.message directly in the HTTP response. In production, stack traces leak implementation details and internal file paths to clients.

WHAT: Update errorHandler.ts to:
1. Only include err.stack in the console.error call (already there), but never send the stack in the HTTP response.
2. When NODE_ENV === 'production', replace err.message with a generic 'Internal Server Error' for 5xx responses while still logging the real error server-side.
3. For 4xx errors (err.status < 500), continue returning err.message since those are intentional user-facing messages.
4. Keep the err.details / err.errorDetails passthrough as-is (useful for validation errors).

Acceptance criteria:
- In production mode, a 500 response body contains `{ message: 'Internal Server Error' }` not the raw error message.
- In development mode, err.message is still surfaced for easier debugging.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

title: Add graceful shutdown handler to index.ts
description:
WHY: backend/src/index.ts calls app.listen() but never handles SIGTERM or SIGINT. When Kubernetes sends SIGTERM to drain a pod, in-flight requests are dropped immediately. A graceful shutdown handler allows the server to stop accepting new connections while completing existing requests.

WHAT: After app.listen() resolves, attach process.on('SIGTERM') and process.on('SIGINT') handlers that:
1. Call server.close() to stop accepting new connections.
2. Wait for in-flight requests to drain (with a 10-second hard timeout).
3. Close the TypeORM AppDataSource connection.
4. Call process.exit(0) on clean shutdown or process.exit(1) on timeout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sending SIGTERM to the running process results in a clean exit with code 0 after in-flight requests complete.
- The TypeORM data source is explicitly destroyed before exit.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

Files to touch:
- backend/src/index.ts

title: Add request ID middleware for distributed tracing
description:
WHY: When a request fails, there is no correlation ID to tie a client error report to a specific server log line. This makes debugging production issues slow, especially with multiple backend replicas behind a load balancer.

WHAT: Create backend/src/middlewares/requestId.ts. The middleware should:
1. Read the X-Request-ID header if present (forwarded by the load balancer or client).
2. Generate a UUID v4 if none is provided (use the built-in crypto.randomUUID()).
3. Attach the id to res.locals.requestId and to req.headers so downstream middleware can read it.
4. Set X-Request-ID on the response.
Register it in app.ts as the very first middleware (before helmet, cors, morgan).
Update the morgan format string to include :res[x-request-id] so every access log line carries the request ID.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every HTTP response includes an X-Request-ID header.
- If the client sends X-Request-ID, the same value is echoed back.
- If no X-Request-ID is sent, a new UUID is generated.
- Morgan log lines include the request ID.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

title: Add POST /api/auth/refresh token refresh endpoint
description:
WHY: JWTs expire (config.jwt.expiresIn) but there is no way to get a new token without a full re-login. This forces users to log in again on token expiry, which is disruptive. A refresh endpoint allows clients to silently exchange a valid (or recently expired) token for a new one.

WHAT: Add a new handler `refreshToken` in backend/src/controllers/authController.ts. The handler should:
1. Read the Bearer token from the Authorization header (same as authMiddleware).
2. Attempt to verify it with verifyToken; if expired, use jwt.decode() to extract userId without verification (allowing a grace window of up to 7 days past expiry — configure as REFRESH_GRACE_SECONDS env var).
3. Look up the user by userId, return 401 if not found.
4. Issue a new token with generateToken(user.id).
5. Set the cookie and return { token, user } (without password).
Register as POST /api/auth/refresh in routes/auth.ts (no authMiddleware guard — it is the refresh mechanism itself).
Apply the authRateLimiter from br-011.

Acceptance criteria:
- POST /api/auth/refresh with a valid token returns a new token and HTTP 200.
- POST /api/auth/refresh with a token older than the grace window returns HTTP 401.
- POST /api/auth/refresh with a completely invalid/malformed token returns HTTP 401.
- The new token is also set as an httpOnly cookie.
- `cd backend && npm run build` passes.

Files to touch:

- backend/src/routes/auth.ts

description:
WHY: PetSwipe pages have no OpenGraph or Twitter Card meta tags. When users share a link to a pet or the home page on social media, no rich preview (title, description, image) is generated. This reduces click-through from social shares.

WHAT: Use Next.js Head component. For static pages (index, home, faq, adoption-planner, success-stories), add og:title, og:description, og:type: website, og:image (use a static banner image from /public), og:url, twitter:card: summary_large_image. For dynamic pages (pet/[id].tsx), generate og:title from the pet name, og:description from the pet description (truncated to 160 chars), og:image from the pet photoUrl. Create a reusable SeoHead component in frontend/components/SeoHead.tsx to avoid repeating Head tags. Place the banner image at frontend/public/og-banner.png.

Acceptance criteria:
- All static pages have og:title, og:description, og:image.
- The pet detail page has dynamic OG tags using the pet's data.
- twitter:card is set to summary_large_image on all pages.
- Paste a URL into a social preview tool (e.g., opengraph.xyz) and see a rich card.
- `cd frontend && npm run build` passes.
